question.text: A knot is held in place by three strings. String C runs horizontally from the knot to a wall. String B runs from the knot up to the ceiling, making a 30° angle with the vertical. String A hangs vertically down from the knot and supports a block of mass 10 kg. The whole system is in equilibrium. Which string has zero tension?
conditions: string C is horizontal, tied to a wall
string B is tied to the ceiling, making a 30° angle with the ceiling
string A is vertical and supports the 10 kg block
mass of the block is 10 kg

figure.description: A vertical wall on the left and a horizontal ceiling meet at a corner. From a common knot below and to the right of the corner, string C runs horizontally to the left to the wall, string B runs up and to the right to the ceiling making a 30° angle with the vertical dashed line through the knot (so 60° with the ceiling), and string A hangs straight down from the knot, holding a 10 kg block at its bottom end.

solution.approach: Balance the knot vertically and horizontally to find all three string tensions, then check whether any of them actually comes out zero.

steps.text: At the knot, three strings pull: A straight down carrying the 10 kg block, B up to the ceiling at 30° from the vertical, and C straight toward the wall (horizontal).
Balance the vertical direction; only T(A) and the vertical part of T(B) act vertically.
Balance the horizontal direction; only T(C) and the horizontal part of T(B) act horizontally.
All three tensions come out clearly positive, so none of the strings carries zero tension.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming a horizontal string like C carries no load since it does not hold up any weight directly, missing that it must balance the horizontal pull of the angled string B.
